| Claim | Verified |

One thing the card does not mention that raises the stakes slightly: **`isOrganizationScopedUnique` is exported from `index.ts:86`**, so this JSDoc is published API documentation — it ships in the `.d.ts` a consumer reads, not just an internal comment. The misleading clause therefore reaches further than the file it sits in.

### The one-vote veto on this card

The tempting edit — routing the declared-index branch through the helper to make code and comment agree — is **option 1 of #8323, which the maintainer rejected**, and it would pre-empt the bare-spelling question parked on **#5082**. It would silently reinterpret every declared `unique: true` on deployed databases as organization-scoped: an unannounced index migration, landing a release *before* #5082 refuses the spelling, producing exactly the two-migrations-two-contradictory-meanings sequence the ruling exists to avoid.

The dispatch carries that as a stop-and-report-a-fork condition. This card corrects the **comment**, and only the comment.

## ACCEPT — holding the ready-flip until CI converges

Reviewed against the branch and `origin/main` @ `8c8f0df`, ⛔ not against the report. PR #8512, 2 files, **+51 / −3** (the 3 deletions are the old JSDoc lines it replaces).

### The one-vote veto held

`normalizeDeclaredIndex` is **not in the diff**, the helper body is unchanged, and neither call site moved. The apparent inconsistency the card is about is still there — which is the correct outcome, and the whole point.

### The comment now repels the edit rather than merely not inviting it

That was the part I added to the dispatch beyond the card's "one-line doc correction", and it's the part that makes this worth a PR. The new text doesn't just scope the helper to field-level; it records **why** the divergence is right and what breaks if someone unifies it — the rejected option 1 of #8323, the silent reinterpretation of every deployed declared `unique: true`, and the two-migrations-with-contradictory-meanings sequence that lands if it precedes #5082. A reader arriving with a tidy-up in mind now learns the hazard instead of re-deriving it.

### Citations verified independently — I checked these before the report arrived

| Cited | Verified on `origin/main` |

| pin `sql-driver-declared-index-organization-respelling.test.ts` | exists ✅ |
| lint `unique/unscoped-declared-index` in `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts` | 2 hits ✅ (dev locates the rule id at `:101`, contract at `:137-141`) |
| `IndexSchema.unique`'s `describe()` in `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` | `IndexSchema` at `:372`, describe at `:401` ✅ |

Neither anchor had moved, which is what I asked it to confirm rather than assume.

### Changeset `patch` — and this time the `.d.ts` claim is proven, not argued

I warned it not to copy #8283's reasoning, since that precedent covered a `protected` member and this is a top-level `index.ts` export. It didn't copy: it built the package and found the corrected text **verbatim at `dist/index.d.ts:39-65`, immediately above `declare function isOrganizationScopedUnique`**. That is the empirical version of the argument #8283 made on inference — a better artifact, and worth keeping as the pattern for the next comment-only card in a published package.
